summary: Console SSO completes but users are redirected to approval queue with expired-approval token, blocking login
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users report they complete Okta SSO (successful assertion) but instead of landing in the Console they are redirected to the internal approval queue page with an error: "Approval token expired". This prevents them from finishing login and accessing internal tools.

Impact: Multiple engineers and support staff in us-east are blocked from Console access for admin/operational workflows. Affects daily runbooks and oncall rotations; currently blocking access to incident dashboards for a subset (~8-12) of users. Not customer-facing but high business impact.

Environment: prod-us-east, identity-proxy v2.9.1, authz-service v1.4.3, console webapp v3.2.0. Okta tenant: redwood-prod.okta.com. Device trust is enabled for affected users.

Steps to reproduce (observed intermittently):
1) User clicks "Sign in with Okta" from Console login.
2) Okta authentication completes (user receives 200 on callback endpoint).
3) Console redirects to /internal/approval-queue?token=<opaque> and shows message: "Approval token expired".
4) No useful error in browser console beyond 403 on /api/approval/validate.

Observed behavior:
- Okta logs show successful SAML/OIDC assertion for the user.
- Identity-proxy logs show callback processing completed and a token exchange call to authz-service.
- Authz-service intermittently returns 401/403 for token validation with body: "token not found or expired".
- Affected users often have recently rotated device attestation certificates or are on corporate-managed laptops (device-trust flow).

Expected behavior: After a successful Okta assertion the user should be issued a fresh approval token and be redirected into the console session, bypassing approval-queue unless an explicit manual approval is required.

Logs / evidence:
- Identity-proxy request-id: ip-req-20260314-7a2f (attached in ticket thread).
- Authz-service trace (2026-03-14T15:22:11Z): 401 response to /validate with message "approval token stale: lease not found".
- Okta logs (2026-03-14T15:21:58Z): assertion processed, code=SUCCESS, subject=alice@redwood.com.
- Browser capture shows redirect to /internal/approval-queue?token=exp_1612345678.

Temporary workaround: Users can open an incognito window and re-try sign-in; some succeed when proxy route lands on a different authz-service replica. As a temporary mitigation we added a sticky session bypass for identity-proxy to route authn callbacks to the freshest authz instance (manual change) which restored access for a few affected users.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Race between token minting and distributed lease propagation in authz-service Redis cluster causing initial tokens to appear expired on validation.
- Hypothesis 2: Identity-proxy is sending a stale/legacy approval token ID when device-trust header is present due to header-name normalization change in v2.9.1.
- Hypothesis 3: An authz-service eviction job runs at 5m intervals and may prematurely evict short-lived approval tokens when system clock skew exists on one replica.

Initial findings:
- We replicated the flow in staging and saw a 5% failure rate when authz-service had high GC pauses; failures correlated to one replica with ntp drift of ~7s.
- Redis AOF showed token leases created then deleted by eviction script within 2s on one shard.

Immediate next steps:
1) SRE to check NTP drift and restart the authz-service replica with skew > 2s (in progress).
2) Temporarily increase approval token TTL to 60s from 15s while we observe in prod (change request opened).
3) Engineering to patch identity-proxy header normalization edge-case in v2.9.1 (PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412).
4) Add additional logging around token mint + validate pair to capture request-ids end-to-end.

Follow-ups: If token TTL increase reduces incidents we will roll permanent fix around lease propagation and remove the sticky bypass route.
